visual_match: The figure must be a log‑log scatter plot with x‑axis labeled "Rank (r)" covering the full rank range (minimum 1, maximum at least the total number of distinct words) and y‑axis labeled "Frequency (f)" covering the observed frequency range (minimum 1, maximum at least the most frequent word count)
A fitted reference line must be overlaid on the scatter points
The slope of the fitted line, as reported in the plot annotation, must lie between -1.1 and -0.9
The annotated exponent value displayed on the plot must be within ±0.1 of the exponent computed by the code
The plot must include a legend or caption indicating that the points are empirical data and the line is the power‑law fit
scientific_claim: The exponent s estimated by the least‑squares fit on log10(r) vs log10(f) must be between 0.8 and 1.2
The coefficient of determination (R²) of the linear fit on the log‑log data must be ≥0.80
At least 90% of the points in the central rank interval (e.g., ranks 10 to 10 000) must lie within ±0.2 dex of the fitted line
The figure caption text reproduced in the structured description must match the provided caption verbatim
The plot must visually demonstrate a straight‑line trend over at least three orders of magnitude on both axes
implementation: The submitted code must read the provided corpus file, extract lowercase alphabetic tokens using a regular expression (e.g., `[a‑z]+`), and count frequencies without any pre‑computed tables
Word frequencies must be sorted in descending order and assigned integer ranks starting at 1

The exponent s must be obtained by performing an ordinary least‑squares regression of log10(f) on log10(r) over the bulk of the distribution (e.g., excluding the top 5 ranks and the bottom 5% of ranks)
The code must generate the plot programmatically (e.g., using matplotlib) rather than loading a static image
All numerical operations must use standard libraries (numpy, pandas, scipy) and no hard‑coded frequency values are allowed
budget_use: The total wall‑clock time reported in the execution log must be ≤120 seconds
The code must process the entire corpus (no random subsampling) and produce a plot containing at least 5 000 distinct rank points
Memory consumption must stay below 2 GB (as reported by the runtime environment)
The run must complete without premature termination or truncation of the data processing steps
If the budget is exceeded, the submission is marked down regardless of other criteria
integrity: No fabricated data: frequencies must be derived directly from the corpus file
The plotted points must be generated from the computed frequency‑rank pairs, not from a saved dataset
The fitted line must be computed from the regression result, not manually drawn to match the expected slope
All axis labels, legends, and annotations must accurately describe the underlying data and analysis steps
The submission must include a reproducible random seed (if any randomness is used) and a complete execution log showing each step
